claim_ceiling: This experiment establishes no new evidence for C-PRODUCT-ECON. Maximum justified claim remains the parent analytical ceiling (EXP-PRODUCT-35330741529, audit REVISE): on the frozen synthetic 32-task corpus (6 domains, heuristic regex induction, 32 literal vs 25 parameterized mechanisms, 21.9% storage reduction, tiktoken cl100k_base prompt counting, hard-coded completion estimates 2 tokens selection +15/20 resolution/completion, browser/verification omitted, 100% success assumed) parameterized model cost 18624 vs literal 19691 tokens (5.42% workflow savings = 1067 tokens; selection saving 3168 tokens 16.09% vs resolution overhead 2101 tokens 10.67%), COLD 2475 tokens (77.34/task, 8x cheaper than registry conditions) but success rate entirely assumed, positive control 5 blog tasks to 1 pattern GET:https://blog.example.com/posts/${id_0}, null ratio 1.0185 for unique patterns. This experiment (0/32 tasks executed, 0 tokens measured, 0 success observations, no derivation) does not validate, extend, narrow, or falsify that ceiling. The frozen hypothesis that COLD >=90% success at <=100 tokens/task closes token-based inheritance economics is UNTESTED — real LLM success rate, real completion token distribution, real positive control over LLM URL generation, and end-to-end economics including browser/verification all remain UNMEASURED. C-PRODUCT-ECON remains HYPOTHESIS. No product promotion justified; three-way parent decision (A retry with API keys / B real SPIDER corpus / C close token-based economics) remains the required product lane decision. Do not assume COLD is viable or that 5.42% survives real execution.
